skill.name: aws-compliance-checker
skill.description: Guides AWS compliance checks for CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2 using AWS CLI and boto3 examples.
skill.summary: Audit AWS environments against common security and compliance controls with AWS CLI and boto3 examples.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden network callbacks. The static findings are documented AWS compliance-check examples, documentation links, and benchmark checks for public network exposure rather than malicious execution paths.

remediation.issue: Runnable examples query AWS account metadata and can reveal sensitive resource details.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to run checks with read-only credentials and protect generated output as internal security evidence.

remediation.issue: The skill front matter labels risk as safe despite extensive AWS CLI and boto3 examples.
remediation.suggestion: Document that the skill uses external commands and AWS API queries so users can approve execution intentionally.

remediation.issue: Some reporting functions are placeholders rather than complete compliance logic.
remediation.suggestion: Mark placeholder sections clearly or provide complete implementations before recommending production automation.

content.value_statement: AWS compliance reviews require many service checks across identity, logging, networking, and encryption. This skill provides structured AWS CLI and boto3 examples for common frameworks.
actual_capabilities: Provides CIS AWS Foundations checks for IAM, logging, monitoring, and networking controls.
Shows AWS CLI checks for root MFA, password policy, CloudTrail, AWS Config, S3 logging, and VPC Flow Logs.
Includes PCI-DSS and HIPAA examples using boto3 and AWS CLI.
Identifies internet-open SSH and RDP security group rules.
Generates a simple framework score and local compliance report example.
Lists prompts for CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2, and dashboard tasks.
limitations: Requires valid AWS credentials and permissions before checks can return useful results.
Examples are not a complete substitute for a formal compliance audit.
Some report functions are placeholders and need implementation before production use.
Command output may expose account details, resource names, and access key identifiers.

use_cases.title: Validate AWS Baselines
use_cases.description: Review common identity, logging, monitoring, networking, and encryption controls before an internal audit.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect structured readiness notes for CIS, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, or SOC 2 control reviews.

use_cases.title: Add Recurring Posture Checks
use_cases.description: Adapt the example commands into scheduled reviews for cloud operations and remediation tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Run a CIS Baseline Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to review CIS AWS Foundations controls for my AWS account. Explain required AWS permissions before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Check Logging Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to assess CloudTrail, AWS Config, S3 access logging, and VPC Flow Logs. Summarize failed controls.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare PCI Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker to create a PCI-DSS readiness summary for network exposure, encryption, MFA, and CloudTrail coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-compliance-checker findings to group failed AWS controls by framework, owner, severity, and remediation priority.

output_examples.input: Run CIS AWS Foundations compliance check
output_examples.output: A sectioned IAM, logging, monitoring, and networking review with pass, warning, and failure messages.
A report summary listing failed payment security controls such as open security groups, unencrypted storage, and missing MFA.

output_examples.input: Check HIPAA compliance for my AWS account
output_examples.output: A review of access controls, audit logging, encryption at rest, and transmission security reminders.

best_practices: Run checks with least-privilege, read-only AWS credentials.
Store generated reports in approved locations because they may contain account details.
Validate findings with AWS Security Hub, AWS Config, or a qualified auditor.
anti_patterns: Do not run the scripts with broad administrator credentials unless required by policy.
Do not publish raw reports because they may reveal resource names and control gaps.
Do not treat placeholder report functions as production-ready automation.

faq.question: Does this skill change AWS resources?
faq.answer: The examples primarily describe read-only checks. Review commands before use and avoid adding remediation actions without approval.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It references CIS AWS Foundations, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC 2, with stronger examples for CIS, PCI-DSS, and HIPAA.

faq.question: What tools are needed?
faq.answer: The examples use AWS CLI, jq, shell utilities, and boto3 for Python examples.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it enough for formal certification?
faq.answer: No. It can support readiness checks, but formal audits require expert review and documented evidence.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: Use least-privilege read access for IAM, CloudTrail, CloudWatch Logs, Config, S3, EC2, RDS, and related services.
